Row.Cell: An M4A1 carbine: gas operated, magazine fed, chambered for 5.56 millimetre ammunition and rifled to throw a small bullet fast and flat. It fires semi automatic or in three round bursts from a thirty round magazine, and its light metal receiver makes it easy to carry. No idea how I got this.

A compact red dot sight on a rail clamp. Apply it and pick the M4A1 to swap its iron sights for the dot.

The M4A1's flip-up rear sight and front sight post. Apply them and pick the M4A1 to take the red dot sight off and put the iron sights back.

Thirty round M4A1 magazines loaded with 5.56 millimetre cartridges. The count is rounds: the M4 loads thirty at a time and keeps what is left for the next magazine. Far too well made for this century.

Thirty round M4A1 magazines loaded with 5.56 millimetre cartridges. The count is rounds: the M4 loads thirty at a time and keeps what is left for the next magazine. Far too well made for this century.

The M4A1 is a carbine from a far later age. It loads from a magazine instead of the muzzle, so there is no powder to pour and no match to light. It throws a small bullet fast and flat, and fires again as fast as you pull the trigger.
